mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending capacity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates contraction in consumer demand, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and GDPC1 decline, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle contraction regime, a declining industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth momentum falters.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO declines in late-cycle contraction, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A declining housing starts series (HOUST) indicates weakening residential demand, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as broader consumer spending trends deteriorate.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where HOUST declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading exceeding 210.0 indicates accelerating inflation, which typically triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as central banks implement rate hikes to curb price pressures.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 210.0, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market deterioration, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced household income and consumption.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced liquidity conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as equity valuations face pressure from higher discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises in monetary tightening cycles, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
